nodes.name: Overall
nodes.definition: All v12-mapped active evaluation samples.

nodes.name: Recognition
nodes.definition: Attaching semantic labels and identities to what is in the image: category, instance, part, attribute, material, state, action, text and symbol. The question it answers is *what is this*.

nodes.name: Category recognition
nodes.definition: Recognize the semantic category, name, stable identity attribute, or known identity of an object, person, place, or scene.

nodes.name: Part recognition
nodes.definition: Identify or name a sub-part / component of an object (a handle, a wing, an engine bay).

nodes.name: Appearance understanding
nodes.definition: Understand visible appearance in the image plane, including named non-geometric properties and projected 2D shape, silhouette, outline, contour morphology, or edge structure.

nodes.name: Visual similarity
nodes.definition: Judge holistic visual resemblance, difference, or match among complete images, regions, or objects when no localized indexed correspondence and no specific appearance property is requested.

nodes.name: State recognition
nodes.definition: Recognize an ordinary temporary, operational, environmental, or emotional state without judging it against a norm.

nodes.name: Activity understanding
nodes.definition: Understand what activity or event is happening, how it develops, or which semantic stage of an activity or process is shown.

nodes.name: Anomaly detection
nodes.definition: Detect whether an observation departs from what is normal, correct, authentic, healthy, intact, or properly performed.

nodes.name: Situation understanding
nodes.definition: Understand what a whole situation means by combining multiple entities and contextual cues, including relationships, purpose, intent, affordance, safety, and narrative meaning.

nodes.name: OCR and text recognition
nodes.definition: Reading written text, numbers, handwriting, or mathematical expressions rendered in the image, and verifying that a given string is present.

nodes.name: Symbol recognition
nodes.definition: Recognize the conventional meaning of a non-text symbol, icon, pictogram, traffic sign, flag, map key, or legend item.

nodes.name: Region semantic recognition
nodes.definition: Connect semantic concepts to image regions by assigning class labels to pixels or regions across the image.

nodes.name: Reconstruction
nodes.definition: Recovering geometric and photometric scene/image properties: projected 2D spatial arrangement, depth, distance, metric size, orientation, curvature, 3D pose and shape, illumination, and geometry hidden by an occluder. The question it answers is *what is the geometric scene or its projection like*.

nodes.name: Lighting understanding
nodes.definition: Illumination, shading, shadows, highlights, reflectance vs. illumination (intrinsic-image) reasoning, and light-source direction.

nodes.name: Depth understanding
nodes.definition: Recover camera-relative depth or depth order: z/radial distance from the observer, including pairwise front/behind and nearer/farther order along the viewing direction when no physical metric is requested.

nodes.name: Metric 3D relation
nodes.definition: Recover a real-world metric or scale-bearing relation among scene entities: inter-object distance, physical proximity, size, height, length, volume, or quantitative 3D layout.

nodes.name: Occlusion understanding
nodes.definition: Determine whether content is visible, occluded, cropped, or out of frame; recover the occluder/occluded order and causal boundary where one surface blocks another.

nodes.name: 3D shape reasoning
nodes.definition: Reason about intrinsic 3D form that is independent of the observer, including solid identity, congruence, cross-section, folding and unfolding, or local surface bending such as curvature, ridges, and valleys.

nodes.name: Orientation understanding
nodes.definition: Understand the orientation or geometric configuration of a focal entity or visible surface, including heading, facing, gaze, articulated pose, door opening or swing direction, object rotation, relative axis alignment, surface normal, slant, tilt, or slope.

nodes.name: 2D spatial relation
nodes.definition: Understand a directly visible, qualitative spatial relationship in the projected image plane, including position relative to the frame or to another visible entity, without inferring physical depth, metric geometry, or 3D orientation.

nodes.name: Multi-view reasoning
nodes.definition: Transform or integrate camera/observer coordinate frames: camera motion/pose, requested projection, novel view, multi-view layout, or egocentric navigation.

nodes.name: Reorganization
nodes.definition: Organising visual elements into coherent structures without necessarily naming them: grouping and segmentation, correspondence, ordering, counting, localization, and connection/topology. The question it answers is *what goes with what and how is it organised*.

nodes.name: Localization
nodes.definition: Return, select, or evaluate the image support of a target—point, box, crop, mask, polygon, foreground region, or 2D segmentation—regardless of whether the target is an object, part, text, symbol, or interface element.

nodes.name: Connectivity
nodes.definition: Understand whether entities, regions, or graph elements are connected through contact, attachment, containment, support, overlap, adjacency, intersection, a shared carrier, or a traversable path.

nodes.name: Counting
nodes.definition: Count a visually selected set, compare set cardinalities, or derive a fraction, proportion, or percentage from visibly identifiable instances, parts, regions, marks, or text elements.

nodes.name: 2D Ordering
nodes.definition: Recover the original permutation of externally shuffled visual units using spatial or visual continuity.

nodes.name: 2D keypoints
nodes.definition: Recover a predefined image-plane keypoint representation: corners, junctions, salient points, or 2D landmarks.

nodes.name: Visual correspondence
nodes.definition: Establish an explicit localized identity- or function-preserving mapping of a point, patch, part, or entity across indexed images, views, or frames, including tracking and identity-preserving trajectory continuation.

families.name: Recognition

The question it answers is *what is the geometric scene or its projection like*.

leaves.name: Object editing
leaves.definition: Replace an object with one of a requested category in the input image.

sample.question: Swap the corn and tomatoes in the bicycle basket with a bouquet of red roses.

leaves.name: Attribute editing
leaves.definition: Modify a specified appearance attribute, such as color or material, in the input image.

sample.question: Change the black grand piano to a gold finish.

leaves.name: Colorization
leaves.definition: Recover missing chromatic information from an achromatic or color-incomplete image.

sample.question: Colorize the grayscale image with natural, realistic colors.

leaves.name: Z-depth
leaves.definition: Predict camera-axis z-buffer depth for each visible image location.

sample.question: Estimate the depth map of this image.

leaves.name: Euclidean depth
leaves.definition: Predict Euclidean distance from the camera to the visible surface at each image location.

sample.question: Estimate the Euclidean-distance depth map of this image.

leaves.name: Surface normals
leaves.definition: Predict the local three-dimensional surface-normal direction at each image location.

sample.question: Estimate the surface normals of this image.

leaves.name: Principal curvature
leaves.definition: Predict local principal surface curvature from the input image.

sample.question: Estimate the principal curvature map of this image.

leaves.name: Occlusion edges
leaves.definition: Predict image boundaries caused by occlusion and visible depth discontinuities.

sample.question: Detect the occlusion (3D) edges in this image.

leaves.name: 3D keypoints
leaves.definition: Predict a predefined representation of three-dimensional keypoints or landmarks.

sample.question: Generate the 3D keypoint heatmap for this image.

leaves.name: Reshading
leaves.definition: Recover the image's per-pixel shading representation from its visual content.

sample.question: Re-render this image with new lighting (reshading).

leaves.name: Inpainting
leaves.definition: Complete masked rectangular regions of an input image.

sample.question: Inpaint the black rectangular region to reconstruct the complete original image. Keep all visible areas unchanged. Output only the completed image.

leaves.name: Semantic segmentation
leaves.definition: Predict a fixed semantic category label for every image pixel or region.

sample.question: Generate the semantic segmentation map of this image using the fixed COCO 133-category color palette. Assign the same color to all pixels of the same semantic category, including object and background categories. Render unlabeled regions in black. Output only the segmentation map.

leaves.name: 2D edges
leaves.definition: Predict local image-plane edges induced by visible texture and intensity structure.

sample.question: Detect the 2D texture edges in this image.

leaves.name: 2D keypoints
leaves.definition: Predict a predefined representation of two-dimensional image keypoints.

sample.question: Generate the 2D keypoint heatmap for this image.

leaves.name: 2D segmentation
leaves.definition: Partition an image into class-free coherent regions using two-dimensional appearance cues.

sample.question: Produce the 2D unsupervised segmentation of this image.

leaves.name: 2.5D segmentation
leaves.definition: Partition visible surfaces into class-free regions using image and 2.5D geometric cues.

sample.question: Produce the 2.5D unsupervised segmentation of this image.

leaves.name: Object pointing
leaves.definition: Given an image and a category query, overlay one point on every matching visible instance.

sample.question: Mark all gull in this image by placing a dot on each instance.

leaves.name: Jigsaw
leaves.definition: Recover the correct spatial organization of shuffled image regions or patches.

sample.question: Rearrange the shuffled image patches to reconstruct the original image.

leaves.name: Localization
leaves.definition: Mark the image region referred to by a text query.

sample.question:
Locate the object referred to by the text description and mark it with a single clean bounding box.

Referring expression: a smiling bear covered in green moss

leaves.name: Visual similarity

leaves.name: Anomaly detection

Select from the following choices.

leaves.name: Depth understanding
leaves.definition: Recover camera-relative depth or depth order: z/radial distance from the observer, including pairwise front/behind and nearer/farther order along the viewing direction when no physical metric is requested.

choices: A. The sheep is behind the car
B. The sheep is in the front of the car
C. The sheep is on the right of the car
D. The sheep is on the left of the car

leaves.name: Metric 3D relation
leaves.definition: Recover a real-world metric or scale-bearing relation among scene entities: inter-object distance, physical proximity, size, height, length, volume, or quantitative 3D layout.

sample.question:
Is the airplane far away from the bicycle?
Select from the following choices.
sample.reason: Evaluates physical inter-object distance/proximity in the 3D scene ('far away').

leaves.name: 3D shape reasoning

leaves.name: Visual correspondence
leaves.definition: Establish an explicit localized identity- or function-preserving mapping of a point, patch, part, or entity across indexed images, views, or frames, including tracking and identity-preserving trajectory continuation.

sample.question:
Humans can find corresponding points for different objects in the same category. For instance, if there are images of two different cats, then the left ear tip of one cat corresponds to the left ear tip of the other cat, and the right front paw of one cat corresponds to the right front paw of the other cat.
Given the following two images, a reference point is annotated on the first image, labeled with REF. You are given multiple red-circled points on the second image, choices of "A, B, C, D" are drawn beside each circle. Select between the choices on the second image and find the corresponding point for the reference point. Which point is corresponding to the reference point?
Select from the following choices.
sample.reason: Requires establishing semantic point correspondence across two different cow images.
